pr.title: Rename the band to the panel
pr.head: b9e281ac48a170bd7448a1df41c0dec0a20666cb

summary: In Claude Code, the Projector plugin draws a list above the prompt: the pull requests your review and watch loops track, and your inbox of questions and notices that agents post with the ask and tell tools. Until now everything called that list the band. The pull request beneath this one, #336, draws it as one panel on a background of its own, and the owner asked for the feature to be called the panel everywhere, so no reader wonders whether the band and the panel are two things.

This pull request is that rename and nothing else. It changes what people read (the docs, the README, two loop skills), what agents read (the /projector command's description, the inbox tools' descriptions and results, and the agent instructions' template), and the hooks module's code: identifiers, comments, test names, the test file's name, and the keys under which the module stores its state in the Claude Code session. Claude Code's own terms, such as the AbovePrompt site, keep their names, and the earlier sections of the inbox and questions plans keep "band" as their history.

One part of the rename is not cosmetic. The hooks module keeps its state in the session, which outlives a reload or an update of the plugin, and the module now reads that state under new key names. A session that updates therefore starts with empty state, and the panel starts hidden until something shows it. The exception is the record of answers the panel is still delivering. The previous release kept it under bandSending, and losing it would deliver an answer that waits behind a running turn a second time. So the panel moves those entries into panelSending once each time the module loads, and clears the old key.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Panel (formerly the band): the plugin's list above the prompt, of loop pull requests and inbox items.
  • Session state: values the hooks module stores in the Claude Code session through atom, by plugin and key. They survive a reload or an update of the module.
  • Claim: a lease of 60 seconds that project inbox claim gives one deliverer of an answered question, renewed while the delivery waits, so two deliverers never send the same answer.
  • Begin marker: the <!-- projector:begin N --> line that versions the generated block of agent instructions.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• At eb06fe3: changes requested. One finding: after an update, an answer still waiting to be delivered was delivered twice, because nothing read bandSending.
  • At 6fd476e: clean. adoptOldSending takes over the old entries, and the reproduction no longer delivers twice.
  • At b9e281a: clean. Both commits are rebased onto band-as-panel, which now also takes focus away from the panel when a prompt is sent from the terminal. The conflicts were in comments and docs, and that new code reads the renamed isPanelFocused key.
  • Apart from the rename, the tests changed in wording only, plus one new test for the takeover.
  • The gate passed at b9e281a: the Python suite, claude plugin test ., the typecheck, both validations, project check, and git diff --check.

groups.title: The hooks module
groups.kicker: The code that draws the panel, renamed, including the session-state keys it stores
intro: The hooks module, under hooks/, is the TypeScript the Claude Code plugin runs: it draws the panel, registers the inbox tools, and delivers the answers you pick to the agent that asked. Its identifiers, comments, and the strings it shows say "panel" now. The local isPanel, which was true when the surface is a terminal, becomes isTerminal, since every surface now draws the panel.

The module stores its values in the session through atom, and every key but seenLoops is renamed, such as bandSending to panelSending. hooks/types.d.ts declares the keys, and the typecheck fails when the declaration and the atoms disagree. After an update, each renamed key starts from its default. The exception is bandSending, the record of answers the previous release was still delivering. adoptOldSending moves its entries into panelSending before the module renews a claim or settles a submitted answer.

checks.text: Compared the old and new lines of every hooks file with "band" replaced by "panel": the only other changes are the isPanel rename, the reworded comments where "the panel draws as one panel" would repeat itself, and the test constant ENGINE_PANEL, now ENGINE_SITE.

files.note: The panel's hooks: state keys, comments, the strings the tools return, isPanel renamed to isTerminal, and the takeover of bandSending.

checks.text: Without this takeover, a session that updated while an answer waited behind a running turn would let that answer's claim lapse and submit it again. The test from the first review seeds the entry under bandSending and advances 90 seconds. At this head the panel renews the old claim on every tick, submits nothing, and settles the delivery when the old prompt arrives.

The takeover runs before renewClaims reads panelSending, and the prompt hook runs it before it settles a submitted answer, so neither path misses an adopted entry. A takeover that fails runs again on the next call.
isTerminal is the old isPanel: whether the surface is a terminal, which decides the inset, padding, background, header, key hint, and drawer rule.

groups.title: Agent instructions and the Python side
groups.kicker: The generated instructions block moves to version 13, and Python comments follow
intro: project init writes a block of instructions into a repository's AGENTS.md from src/projector/templates/agents-block.md. Its begin marker carries a version, and tests/test_instructions.py pins each version's text by hash, so a change to the text must raise the version. One line of that text named the band, so the block moves to version 13, and this repository's own AGENTS.md is refreshed with it.
In src/projector, only comments and docstrings change.

groups.title: Documentation, skills, and the plan
groups.kicker: What people read says "panel", and the inbox plan records why
intro: The docs and two loop skills say "panel". The headings in docs/plugins.md change, and so do their anchors, such as #read-your-inbox-in-projectors-panel; the README's link follows. The inbox plan, already completed, gains § 21, which records the rename, the reason for it, and the state keys starting fresh after an update.
